subject: Torchlane reserved pool recap & action items
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Choi <samuel.choi@torchlane.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@torchlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T15:05:22-07:00
Subject: Recap: Torchlane capacity discussion — reserved pool & isolation

Sam / Priya — thanks for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps so nothing falls through the cracks. TL;DR: Torchlane needs a reserved GPU pool with tenant isolation for PHI workloads, predictable throughput for spike-prone inference, and an SLA that covers latency and availability for production traffic.

Key pain points you shared:
- PHI and regulatory scope: model outputs feed downstream clinical systems; strict isolation and auditability needed.
- Burstiness: periodic evaluation workloads create 4–6x short-term spikes compared to baseline.
- Predictability: procurement needs a clear committed throughput to justify budget and staffing.

What we heard as goals:
- Committed pool sized for ~250 steady inference RPS (short sequences), able to burst to ~1,000 RPS for 30–60m windows.
- 95p latency SLO of <150ms for typical chat/generation paths at your p95 token lengths.
- End-to-end audit trail (KV cache access logs, request tracing) and SOC2 evidence for vendor security review.

Redwood proposal (high level):
- Dedicated reserved pool: N GPUs (we'll size in follow-up) with VPC isolation and per-tenant encryption.
- Autoscaling/burst policy: reserved baseline plus a burst bucket tied to commit level; automatic fallback to compatible model variant if capacity constrained.
- SLA: availability target + latency SLO; credits model and remediation path in attached draft SLA.

Immediate next steps (owner / target dates):
1) Solutions engineering sizing workshop (30–45m) — owner: Ben Carter — target: 2026-08-24.
2) Draft SLA + MOP + SOC2 summary to be shared — owner: Ava Chen — target: 2026-08-19 (attached SLA + SOC2 summary).
3) Procurement checklist & pricing draft from Ben — owner: Ben Carter — target: 2026-08-21.
4) Legal/contract intro & DPA/standard terms — owner: Marissa Cole — target: 2026-08-26.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sla-draft.pdf (SLA + credit model), torchlane-mop.xlsx (operations footprint template), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (attestation summary).

Questions I still have (will confirm in sizing workshop):
- Typical sequence length distribution for the 95p bucket (short/medium/long)?
- Any hard isolation requirements beyond PHI (e.g., customer-managed key/HSM)?
- Expected monthly token volume for cost modeling.

If this aligns, I'll schedule the sizing workshop with Ben and loop in our solutions engineer. Thanks again — happy to adjust cadence based on your procurement timeline.

—
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182


From: Samuel Choi <samuel.choi@torchlane.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@torchlane.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T17:12:05-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Torchlane capacity discussion — reserved pool & isolation

Thanks Ava — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Sequence distribution: 80% short (<128 tokens), 15% medium (128–512), 5% long (>512). The p95 is usually within the short bucket.
- HSM/KMS: We need the option to use our cloud KMS (customer-managed keys) for a subset of models that serve PHI.
- SOC2: our procurement team will want the full SOC2 Type II report. Your summary is useful but will the full report be shared under NDA / sftp?
- SLA: we care about latency SLOs for synchronous APIs; credits are material to our risk assessment. Also please confirm egress charge assumptions into our cloud region.

We are broadly aligned on the approach. Can we lock the sizing workshop next week? Also, please send the draft DPA/terms we can share with legal.

Best,
Sam
SVP Product, Torchlane
samuel.choi@torchlane.com

Sam — appreciate the fast follow. Short answers inline and next logistics below.

- Sequence mix: thanks, that distribution helps a ton. We'll run sizing scenarios with 80/15/5 and validate the p95 token count in the workshop.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed KMS for volume encryption; for HSM-backed keys we'll confirm options and any additional lead time (likely a short integration step).
- SOC2: full Type II report can be shared after an NDA/secure transfer. I'll sync legal (Marissa) to send the appropriate access steps. The attached redwood-soc2-summary.pdf contains the control mapping procurement typically reviews.
- SLA credits & egress: draft SLA (attached) includes our proposed credit model and a note about egress assumptions — we default to cloud egress as a separate line item, but Ben will model a bundled option in pricing.

Scheduling: Ben is available for a 45m sizing workshop on either 2026-08-24 at 10:00am PT or 2026-08-25 at 2:00pm PT. Which works better?

Attached: redwood-dedicated-sla-draft.pdf, torchlane-mop.xlsx, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

I'll also drop a HubSpot record with the deal skeleton and link to the drive folder here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/TCH-2026-043

- Confirm workshop slot (Sam/Priya) — due: 2026-08-20
- Marissa to start DPA intro and share NDA steps — due: 2026-08-21
- Ben to prepare a pricing model with bundled egress vs line item options — due: 2026-08-21

Date: 2026-08-19T11:42:10-07:00
Subject: Internal: Torchlane procurement & pricing notes (quick)

Ava / Marissa — quick internal note following Sam's ask:

- I'll prepare two pricing scenarios: (A) reserved pool + bundled egress, (B) reserved pool + egress as separate line item. Include a 12-month commit and a 24-month commit variant.
- For the sizing workshop, bring the sample throughput mapping (RPS -> GPUs) and an ops runbook clarifying burst windows. I'll add a short slide on credit math for the SLA.
- Marissa: if we can pre-seed a short DPA + NDA template into DocuSign, that speeds procurement. If legal prefers to own the exact wording, we should at least provide a minimal stub to start the review.

I'll have a tight draft of pricing + slide deck to you both by end of day Friday (2026-08-21).

—
